title: ACCOUNTABILITY
mv: Then David spoke to the LORD when he saw the angel who was striking the people, and said, "Surely I have sinned, and I have done wickedly; but these sheep, what have they done? Let Your hand, I pray, be against me and against my father's house.
mvp: ‘‘Then David spoke to the LORD when he saw the angel who was striking the people, and said, "Surely I have sinned, and I have done wickedly; but these sheep, what have they done? Let Your hand, I pray, be against me and against my father's house.’’ 2 Samuel 24:17 (NKJV)
assignment: List five (5) key areas where you need accountability (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: Accountability is the acknowledgement by an individual, a group, an organisation, etc., that they are responsible for their actions. It is being answerable to yourself, others and God, for your actions, inactions, contributions and impact. This lesson shall examine ways to be accountable as an individual and organisation, and the pluses of such actions.

As individuals, we must be accountable to ourselves by taking responsibility for our actions without shifting blame to others (Galatians 6:4-5). We should be truthful to ourselves, follow through on our commitments and align our choice with our values (Hosea 10:12). We must also grow to have accountability partners; always have someone you report to, discuss with and brainstorm together (Proverbs 27:17). It is necessary to have a good voice over our head; the person who can challenge and correct us (James 5:16a). Since nothing is hidden from God, let us note that every one of us shall give account of himself to Him (Hebrews 4:13; Romans 14:12). Organisations must deliberately build a culture of accountability in their corporation. Employees must be responsible for their actions and performance in achieving the organisation’s vision and mission statement. To achieve the organisation’s goal, there should be transparency, a friendly environment, and fair play.

Being accountable comes with a lot of advantages to us as individuals and even to organisations. As individuals, it helps us to be confident (1 Samuel 12:3; 2 Timothy 4:6-8), delegate tasks (Exodus 18:20-22), set goals, and reward success. We also become resilient (Romans 5:3-4). Accountability helps us to learn from our mistakes and become better at what we do. It also aids us to grow our careers, earn trust and respect in our relationships (Daniel 5:10-12).

As an organisation, accountability cultivates trust, increases productivity, and drives higher performance throughout the company (Matthew 24:45-47). It also grows investors’ confidence while the company will enjoy improved returns. Also, employees’ loyalty is gained through proper accountability, as they are assured of better treatment. The general outlook of the company is seen in a positive light when it is accountable.
Being accountable helps us to stay off the blame game and take responsibility (2 Samuel 24:10).
Be accountable and stop trading blame.
